title: Summary Of The Lesson From The Cosmos There Is No God But Allah

questions.question: What main truth is seen among the things in the universe in this passage?
questions.answer: A strong pattern of helping and working together is seen among them.

questions.question: What are beings in the passage trying to keep?
questions.answer: They are trying to keep their existence, and living things are also trying to keep their life.

questions.question: What else are these beings trying to do besides stay alive?
questions.answer: They are also carrying out their jobs or purposes.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the changes happening around them?
questions.answer: The changes are constant and full of movement and turning.

questions.question: Why is this co-operation surprising?
questions.answer: It goes far beyond what those beings could do by themselves.

questions.question: Which group is said to help living creatures directly?
questions.answer: The basic materials of the world, like the elements, are said to help living creatures.

questions.question: What do the clouds help?
questions.answer: They help plants grow.

questions.question: What do plants help?
questions.answer: They help animals.

questions.question: What do animals help?
questions.answer: They help human beings.

questions.question: What example is given to show mercy toward babies?
questions.answer: Milk is provided for a baby in a gentle and caring way.

questions.question: From where are living things sometimes given what they need?
questions.answer: They are given it from places they would not expect.

questions.question: What happens to food inside the body according to the passage?
questions.answer: Tiny food particles are directed to renew and supply the body’s cells.

questions.question: What do these examples of co-operation show about the Lord of the worlds?
questions.answer: They show His rule is wide-reaching and full of mercy.

questions.question: What picture is used to explain how the universe is managed?
questions.answer: It is compared to a palace being run and cared for.

questions.question: Why can lifeless things not be the real planners of this co-operation?
questions.answer: Because they have no feeling or awareness, yet they act in fitting and careful ways.

questions.question: According to the passage, by whose power and command do such things help one another?
questions.answer: They do so by the power, mercy, and command of a wise, glorious, and compassionate Lord.

questions.question: What other big signs in the universe are named along with co-operation?
questions.answer: Balance, protection, beauty, order, and giving duties are also named.

questions.question: How wide is the balance and preservation described in the passage?
questions.answer: It covers everything from huge planets down to body parts and even tiny particles.

questions.question: What does the passage say about beauty in creation?
questions.answer: Beauty appears across the sky, the earth, and even delicate flowers.

questions.question: What does the passage say about assigned duties?
questions.answer: It says all kinds of things, from great heavenly bodies to bees, are given tasks.

questions.question: What is the role of these truths in the testimony of the universe?
questions.answer: They make up the second wing of the universe’s witness.

questions.question: Why does the passage end with only a short treatment of this topic?
questions.answer: Because it says this proof has already been explained clearly elsewhere, so only a brief sign is given here.

questions.question: What truth is the passage focusing on in the universe?
questions.answer: It focuses on the truth that created things support one another.

questions.question: In what situation do these beings show co-operation?
questions.answer: They show it while trying to continue existing, living, and doing their work during ongoing change.

questions.question: How do the elements behave toward living things?
questions.answer: They quickly serve and help them.

questions.question: How do the clouds serve the world of plants?
questions.answer: They aid plants by supporting their growth.

questions.question: How does the plant world serve the animal world?
questions.answer: Plants become a support and benefit for animals.

questions.question: How does the animal world serve human beings?
questions.answer: Animals provide help and benefit for people.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about how living things receive provision?
questions.answer: They receive what they need in ways beyond their own ability and often from unexpected places.

questions.question: What example from inside the body shows organized help?
questions.answer: Food particles are directed to the body’s cells to renew and feed them.

questions.question: What do these many examples prove about the One who manages the universe?
questions.answer: They prove that His care and lordship reach everything with mercy.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the universe under this management?
questions.answer: It is likened to a palace under careful control.

questions.question: Why is the co-operation of lifeless things a proof rather than an accident?
questions.answer: Because objects without awareness still act as if they know where help is needed.

questions.question: What must be behind the helpful actions of these unfeeling things?
questions.answer: The will and command of a merciful and wise Sustainer must be behind them.

questions.question: Name two broad patterns in the cosmos besides co-operation that point to this Sustainer.
questions.answer: Two examples are balance and preservation.

questions.question: How far does this balance extend?
questions.answer: It extends from the stars and planets to the tiny parts inside living bodies.

questions.question: Where does the passage say adornment or beauty can be seen?
questions.answer: It can be seen in the sky, on the earth, and on flowers.

questions.question: What examples are given to show order in all sizes of creation?
questions.answer: Great systems in space and fruits like corn and pomegranates are both mentioned.

questions.question: What examples are given to show that many things receive duties?
questions.answer: The sun, moon, elements, clouds, and honey-bees are all named.

questions.question: In the passage, this testimony is called the second wing of what?
questions.answer: It is called the second wing of the testimony of the cosmos.

questions.question: Why is only a brief explanation given at the end?
questions.answer: Because the fuller explanation is said to have already been made elsewhere.

questions.question: What is one main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: Everything in creation is linked by a pattern of mutual help.

questions.question: Besides survival, what are beings also doing?
questions.answer: They are fulfilling the roles given to them.

questions.question: What makes the co-operation mentioned here amazing?
questions.answer: It keeps happening during nonstop changes and is greater than the beings’ own ability.

questions.question: What is the first chain of help described in the examples?
questions.answer: Materials of the world help living things, clouds help plants, plants help animals, and animals help people.

questions.question: How does the passage show kindness toward infants?
questions.answer: It mentions that their food is provided in a tender and fitting way.

questions.question: What can we learn from the fact that creatures get provision from unexpected places?
questions.answer: Their needs are being cared for by more than their own effort.

questions.question: What happens to food particles inside the body?
questions.answer: They are guided to the cells to support and renew them.

questions.question: What bigger truth do all these examples point to?
questions.answer: They point to the merciful care and rule of the Lord of all worlds.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare the cosmos to a palace?
questions.answer: To show that it is run in an organized, planned, and caring way.

questions.question: What problem would come if someone claimed lifeless things organize this help by themselves?
questions.answer: That would mean unaware things act with understanding and care, which does not fit their nature.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from the helpful actions of lifeless things?
questions.answer: A compassionate and wise Sustainer directs them.

questions.question: Which quality in the universe means things are kept in proper measure?
questions.answer: Equilibrium or balance.

questions.question: Which quality means things are guarded and maintained?
questions.answer: Preservation.

questions.question: How regular are balance and preservation said to be?
questions.answer: They are described as being present with the highest regularity.

questions.question: Give one large example and one small example used to show order.
questions.answer: A large example is the heavenly systems, and a small example is fruit such as corn or pomegranate.

questions.question: What does the mention of flowers add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that even delicate and beautiful things are carefully decorated.

questions.question: What does the mention of bees show?
questions.answer: It shows that even small creatures are given duties.

questions.question: What do all these truths together offer?
questions.answer: They offer a powerful witness pointing to the One who manages everything.

questions.question: What place does this witness have in the overall witness of the universe?
questions.answer: It is the second part, called the second wing.

questions.question: Does the passage present this as a weak sign or a great testimony?
questions.answer: It presents it as a great testimony.

questions.question: Why does the speaker stop after a short explanation?
questions.answer: Because a detailed explanation is said to be available in the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What kind of relationship among created things is described at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: A relationship of support and mutual help.

questions.question: What are all these beings struggling to maintain?
questions.answer: Their existence, and if they are alive, their life as well.

questions.question: What does the passage say about their ability compared to the help we observe?
questions.answer: The observed help is beyond what they could manage on their own.

questions.question: How do the elements act toward living creatures?
questions.answer: They move to assist them.

questions.question: What is the role of clouds in the passage?
questions.answer: They serve the plant world.

questions.question: What is the role of plants in the passage?
questions.answer: They serve the animal world.

questions.question: What is the role of animals in the passage?
questions.answer: They serve human beings.

questions.question: Which example especially highlights care for the weakest humans?
questions.answer: The feeding of babies through milk.

questions.question: What does it mean that provision comes from “unexpected places”?
questions.answer: It means creatures receive what they need without being able to fully plan or produce it themselves.

questions.question: How does the body give another sign of co-operation?
questions.answer: Food particles are made to serve the cells of the body.

questions.question: What do these examples show about the One who provides and manages?
questions.answer: They show that He rules with mercy over all worlds.

questions.question: Why is the palace image a helpful comparison?
questions.answer: Because a palace suggests planning, care, arrangement, and management by one ruler.

questions.question: What are lifeless objects called in the passage besides being solid?
questions.answer: They are described as without life and feeling.

questions.question: If they have no awareness, how can they still seem to help in fitting ways?
questions.answer: They are being directed by the power and command of the Sustainer.

questions.question: Which divine qualities are named in connection with this directing?
questions.answer: Mercy, wisdom, and glory are named.

questions.question: What universal pattern is said to be visible throughout the cosmos?
questions.answer: Co-operation everywhere.

questions.question: What two qualities are said to be found from planets down to tiny body parts?
questions.answer: Balance and preservation.

questions.question: In what places is adornment or decoration seen?
questions.answer: In the heavens, the earth, and flowers.

questions.question: What examples show that order exists in both huge and small things?
questions.answer: The starry systems above and fruits below both show it.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the jobs of things like the sun, moon, clouds, and bees?
questions.answer: Each has duties assigned to it.

questions.question: How do these many signs function together?
questions.answer: Together they form a major witness from the universe.

questions.question: What name is given to this major witness within the whole testimony of the cosmos?
questions.answer: It is called the second wing.

questions.question: Why is the discussion kept short here?
questions.answer: Because the author says the matter has already been established and explained elsewhere.

questions.question: According to the passage, what truth can be clearly noticed among beings in the world?
questions.answer: They show a real pattern of working together.

questions.question: What are these beings busy doing while this co-operation happens?
questions.answer: They are trying to continue existing, keep living if alive, and complete their tasks.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the many changes happening around them?
questions.answer: These changes are always taking place.

questions.question: Why is the co-operation called a truth beyond their capacities?
questions.answer: Because the beings themselves do not have enough power or awareness to arrange all of it.

questions.question: How do the basic elements serve living things?
questions.answer: They hurry to help them.

questions.question: How do clouds fit into the chain of help?
questions.answer: They support plants.

questions.question: How do plants fit into the chain of help?
questions.answer: They support animals.

questions.question: How do animals fit into the chain of help?
questions.answer: They support human beings.

questions.question: What example is given to show gentle provision for a baby?
questions.answer: A baby is nourished with milk provided in a merciful way.

questions.question: What is important about the way creatures receive their provision?
questions.answer: They receive it in ways above their own strength and often from places they did not expect.

questions.question: What small-scale example inside the body shows organized care?
questions.answer: Food particles are sent to body cells to renew them.

questions.question: What do all these examples teach about the Lord of all the worlds?
questions.answer: They teach that His care is universal and full of compassion.

questions.question: What does managing the cosmos “like a palace” suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests wise control, order, and purposeful care.

questions.question: Why can’t unfeeling objects be the true source of this careful co-operation?
questions.answer: Because they do not have the awareness needed to choose and help so fittingly.

questions.question: Then what must be making them aid one another?
questions.answer: The command and power of a compassionate and wise Sustainer.

questions.question: What large pattern besides co-operation is seen everywhere in creation?
questions.answer: A pattern of balance.

questions.question: What does preservation mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means things are protected and maintained in an orderly way.

questions.question: From what to what does this balance and preservation extend?
questions.answer: From the planets down to limbs, organs, and tiny particles in living bodies.

questions.question: Where is beauty or adornment seen according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is seen across the sky, the earth, and flowers.

questions.question: What examples show that order reaches both space and the earth?
questions.answer: It reaches great systems like the Milky Way and small fruits like corn and pomegranates.

questions.question: What does the passage say about duty in creation?
questions.answer: Many things, big and small, are given jobs to do.

questions.question: Which small creature is mentioned as having a duty?
questions.answer: The honey-bee.

questions.question: How important is this testimony from co-operation and order?
questions.answer: It is one of the two great wings of the universe’s witness.

questions.question: Why does the passage not go into more detail?
questions.answer: Because it says the topic has already been made clear in other writings.

questions.question: What truth does the passage say can be seen among beings in the universe?
questions.answer: A truth of mutual help and co-operation.

questions.question: What three things are these beings trying to do in the middle of change?
questions.answer: They are trying to remain in existence, keep their life if they are animate, and perform their functions.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the changes around them?
questions.answer: It describes them as continual and full of upheaval.

questions.question: What does it mean that this co-operation is beyond their capacities?
questions.answer: It means they cannot fully produce or organize it by themselves.

questions.question: Which things are said to rush to help living creatures?
questions.answer: The elements.

questions.question: Which part of creation helps the plant world?
questions.answer: The clouds.

questions.question: Which part of creation helps the animal world?
questions.answer: The plant world.

questions.question: Which part of creation helps the human world?
questions.answer: The animal world.

questions.question: What example shows special mercy to an infant?
questions.answer: The infant is fed with milk in a way full of care.

questions.question: What lesson comes from creatures receiving their needs from unexpected places?
questions.answer: Their provision is being arranged for them.

questions.question: What happens to food particles in the body?
questions.answer: They are made to serve the cells and renew them.

questions.question: What do these examples together demonstrate?
questions.answer: They demonstrate the all-encompassing and merciful lordship of the Sustainer of all worlds.

questions.question: Why is the universe compared to a palace?
questions.answer: Because it is governed in an organized and intentional way.

questions.question: What is striking about the behavior of lifeless and unfeeling things?
questions.answer: They still seem to act in careful, fitting, almost aware ways.

questions.question: What conclusion should be drawn from that striking behavior?
questions.answer: They are being directed by a compassionate, wise, and glorious Sustainer.

questions.question: What other universal reality is mentioned right after co-operation?
questions.answer: A widespread state of balance and preservation.

questions.question: How broad is this balance in creation?
questions.answer: It includes everything from planets to the smallest bodily parts.

questions.question: What does the passage say about adornment?
questions.answer: It says beauty is spread over the heavens, the earth, and flowers.

questions.question: What does the passage say about order?
questions.answer: It says order rules over everything from giant star systems to small fruits.

questions.question: What does the passage say about duties in creation?
questions.answer: It says duties are assigned to all sorts of things, from the sun and moon to bees.

questions.question: Why is mentioning both very large things and very small things important?
questions.answer: It shows that the same wise rule covers all levels of creation.

questions.question: What do all these truths provide together?
questions.answer: They provide a great testimony.

questions.question: What is this testimony called in relation to the cosmos?
questions.answer: It is called the second wing of the cosmos’s testimony.

questions.question: Why is the final statement so brief?
questions.answer: Because the passage says this testimony has already been explained and proven elsewhere.
